issues.label: Problem 1
issues.status: Demonstrated mean-compatibility defect; local algebraic repair proved.
issues.hypotheses: Normalized torus measure, nonnegative translated partition chi, K=36 covering squares with l=2pi/5, Fourier index set {(1,0),(0,1)}, admissible localization domain/reference square and prescribed return flow. Choose one nonnegative smooth cosine time coefficient supported near the end of the first replayed pause.
issues.suspect_step: Final profiles/coefficients omit the two factors 1/integral chi present in the earlier mean-free control (3.9).
issues.decisive_evidence: Translated partition gives integral chi=1/K. Earlier force eta_hat-(A/c)y dot grad chi-(m/c)chi has zero mean. Printed final force eta_hat-A y dot grad chi-m chi has mean (1-1/K)m. At the end of the first pause Xi approaches x-p_omega on supp chi, with cos Xi1 >= cos(2pi/5)>0; continuity and the allowed coefficient choice give m>0 on a nonempty interval. Printed mean=35m/36>0 there.
counterevidence_and_alternatives: An implicit integral-chi=1 convention contradicts the actual partition identity.
The additional positive rescaling does not remove nonzero mean.
The argument grants time dependence of the y dot grad chi profile, so the demonstrated normalization error does not depend on resolving the separate profile representation issue.
This checks the printed construction for allowed controls; it does not prove nonexistence of some other successful control.

repair.statement: Multiply both correction coefficients by K, or divide both profiles by c=integral chi.
repair.proof: Substitution recovers exactly the original (3.9) formula, whose integral is m-m=0 since integral y dot grad chi=0.
repair.verified_scope: Mean identity and algebraic agreement only; the entire advertised fixed-profile representation remains unverified.

issues.dependency: Explicit vorticity controls -> Theorem 5.2 -> periodic velocity curl primitive (5.18) -> proof of Theorem 1.1.
issues.severity_basis: The displayed force fails a necessary compatibility condition in the central construction, even though the algebraic normalization can be repaired.

issues.label: Problem 2
issues.status: False regularity scope and bounded-set uniformity demonstrated by exact nonlinear solutions.
issues.hypotheses: nu=m=1, w0=0 in H2, zero prescribed mean path apart from the actual return drift y(t); g,h in L2_t H0 with zero spatial means. Set a(t)=integral y, a(1) in (2pi Z)^2.
issues.suspect_step: Transport is asserted bounded in C H^{m+1} from g in L2 H^{m-1}; the conclusion is H^m convergence uniformly on bounded sets, and the h-tail integral is treated as uniformly small.
issues.decisive_evidence: For g(t,x)=f(x1-a1(t)), h=0, Biot–Savart velocity is vertical, so nonlinear self-advection is exactly zero. v(1)=f and w_delta(delta)=sum b_n F(delta n²)sin(nx1), F(z)=(1-exp(-z))/z. b_n=1/n gives f in H0 not H1, w_delta in H1 and infinite H1 difference for every delta. Smooth g_n=sin(n(x1-a1(t))) with delta_n=n^-2 has bounded L2H0 norm but H1 seminorm error n/(e sqrt2). Independently, g=0 and h_n=n sin(n(x1-a1(t/delta_n))) on (0,delta_n), zero later, have bounded L2H0 norms and endpoint H1 seminorm (1-e^-1)/sqrt2.
counterevidence_and_alternatives: The return drift is retained exactly, not replaced by zero.
Nonlinear self-advection vanishes by the actual shear structure; it is not a linearization.
The constructed controls used later have more spatial regularity and might satisfy a suitably restricted scaling result.
Absolute continuity for a fixed h is distinct from uniformity over a bounded L2 family; source (5.10) is relevant to translated tails of one fixed h.

repair.statement: Restrict to a class with uniform C H^{m+1} bounds on the transported solution and uniform integrability of the h-tail energy.
repair.proof: These are the specific missing controls needed by the printed remainder estimate. A complete corrected uniform theorem over the full claimed class is not asserted.
repair.verified_scope: Exact counterexamples and identification of necessary repair scope; not a replacement general theorem.

issues.dependency: Lemma 4.2 -> Theorem 5.1 scaling -> uniform activation-time argument in Theorem 5.2.
issues.severity_basis: False intermediate guarantee is directly used in the principal proof; no main-theorem refutation is inferred.

issues.label: Problem 3
issues.status: Fixed-control exact-limit assertion contradicted within allowed data.

source_location.claim: Theorem 5.1 fixed L2 controls preceding the delta-to-zero exact-limit quantifier

issues.hypotheses: k=2, w0=0, h=0, nu=1, U=0 and target w1=sum n^-4 sin(nx1), which has zero mean and belongs to H3 but not H4.
issues.suspect_step: Proof chooses an approximation tolerance before selecting controls, while the statement fixes a single control whose delta-to-zero limit is an arbitrary target.
issues.decisive_evidence: For every fixed collection of the stated L2 coefficients, the finite Fourier flow, smooth localization, replay and scalar corrections make g in L2Hq for every q, hence v(1) is smooth. A direct H2 remainder energy inequality E'+delta||grad r||H2² <= C delta(1+E+E²), with E(0)=0, gives E<=3Cdelta on [0,1] by a closed bootstrap. Thus the actual fixed-control limit is smooth v(1). An asserted H2 limit equal to w1 would imply w1=v(1), contradicting w1 notin H4.
counterevidence_and_alternatives: Direct smooth-data limit proof does not rely on the false general form of Lemma 4.2.
Controls depending on epsilon or delta avoid this fixed-control contradiction; those have different quantifiers.
The main theorem asks approximation at a prescribed tolerance, which this counterexample does not contradict.

repair.statement: Use tolerance-dependent controls; for a fixed smooth control, the correct limit of the error norm is ||v(1)-w1||H2.
repair.proof: The direct H2 convergence and continuity of the norm give this precise limit. Approximate transport controllability can make the limit small by choosing a new control.
repair.verified_scope: Fixed-control smooth-data limit and quantifier distinction; no complete uniform replacement across all force classes.

issues.dependency: Theorem 5.1 -> choice of small activation time in Theorem 5.2.
issues.severity_basis: The central intermediate theorem promises an exact limit which its permitted fixed controls cannot supply for allowed nonsmooth targets.

issues.label: Problem 4
issues.status: Literal sufficient observability condition false; strengthened condition proved.
issues.hypotheses: T=1,n=1 and D={d_j} countable dense without repetitions; phi(t)=sum 2^-j 1_{t=d_j}.
issues.suspect_step: Mere discontinuity on a dense set, rather than nonzero jumps, is used to imply an L2 observability statement.
issues.decisive_evidence: phi is bounded/measurable, has both one-sided limits zero everywhere, is continuous off D and discontinuous at each d_j; all stated hypotheses hold. Yet phi=0 almost everywhere, so b=0,a1=1 gives b+a1 phi=0 in L2 without a1=0. Pairwise disjoint dense sets extend the example to larger finite families.
counterevidence_and_alternatives: The hypothesis is about chosen pointwise representatives, while the conclusion is L2; removable discontinuities cannot supply the required jumps.
The subsequent generating-drift theorem separately assumes observability, and valid observable families exist.

repair.statement: Use psi_j(t)=sum 2^-n 1_{t>d_jn} on pairwise disjoint dense sets.
repair.proof: Uniform convergence gives bounded regulated functions with nonzero jumps at their own dense set and continuity at the other sets. In an almost-everywhere zero combination with continuous coefficients, one-sided limits are zero; subtracting at d_jn gives a_j(d_jn)2^-n=0. Density and continuity imply a_j=0, then b=0.
repair.verified_scope: Complete proof for this strengthened construction.

issues.dependency: Local sufficient construction for observable families; not a refutation of the separately assumed observability theorem.
issues.severity_basis: Local overbroad sufficient condition has an explicit direct replacement; no failure of the main approximate-controllability conclusion follows.

unresolved_scope.point: N+1 profile is listed as spatially fixed but contains time-dependent return drift times grad chi.
unresolved_scope.status: Separate representation issue not fully resolved or graded; normalization finding grants the favorable time-dependent interpretation.

unresolved_scope.point: Local change of first spatial mean for a curl-free periodic field.
unresolved_scope.status: If the field changes only inside T times a proper horizontal interval, its horizontal period and first component mean cannot change. This is a bounded unresolved scope observation, not an additional graded finding or a counterexample to Theorem A.1.
